examples.question_text:
For each worker, determine whether there is a tax refund or an amount owing, and state the amount.
(a) Amelia paid $\$8400$ in PAYG instalments and has total tax payable of $\$7650$.
(b) Ben paid $\$6200$ in PAYG instalments and has total tax payable of $\$6980$.
(c) Chen paid $\$5100$ in PAYG instalments and has total tax payable of $\$5100$.
examples.solution_text:
(a)
$\begin{aligned}\text{Balance}&=8400-7650\\&=\$750\end{aligned}$
The instalments exceed the tax payable, so Amelia receives a refund of $\$750.00$.

(b)
$\begin{aligned}\text{Balance}&=6200-6980\\&=-\$780\end{aligned}$
The instalments are less than the tax payable, so Ben owes $\$780.00$.

(c)
$\begin{aligned}\text{Balance}&=5100-5100\\&=\$0\end{aligned}$
The totals are equal, so Chen has neither a refund nor an amount owing.

examples.question_text:
Priya worked for $32$ weeks and had $\$215.50$ withheld from each weekly pay. Her total tax payable for the year is $\$6540$.
Determine her tax refund or amount owing.
examples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned}\text{Total instalments}&=215.50\times32\\&=\$6896\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}\text{Balance}&=6896-6540\\&=\$356\end{aligned}$
Priya paid more than the tax payable, so she receives a refund of $\$356.00$.

examples.question_text:
Marcus has income tax payable of $\$12\,480.60$ and a Medicare levy of $\$1460$. He had $\$520$ withheld from each of his $26$ fortnightly pays.
Determine his tax refund or amount owing.
examples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned}\text{Total tax payable}&=12\,480.60+1460\\&=\$13\,940.60\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}\text{Total instalments}&=520\times26\\&=\$13\,520\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}\text{Balance}&=13\,520-13\,940.60\\&=-\$420.60\end{aligned}$
Marcus has not paid enough tax, so he owes $\$420.60$.

examples.question_text:
Elena's total annual tax payable is $\$14\,456$. She receives $26$ fortnightly pays.
What equal fortnightly PAYG instalment would leave her with neither a refund nor an amount owing?
examples.solution_text:
For neither a refund nor an amount owing, total instalments must equal total tax payable.

$\begin{aligned}\text{Fortnightly instalment}&=14\,456\div26\\&=\$556.00\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text:
Noah has an annual taxable income of $\$58\,600$. He had $\$350$ withheld from each of his $26$ fortnightly pays.
For taxable incomes from $\$45\,001$ to $\$120\,000$, the supplied tax table gives income tax of $\$5092$ plus $32.5$ cents for each dollar over $\$45\,000$.
Use this table rule to determine his tax refund or amount owing. Ignore the Medicare levy.
examples.solution_text:
His taxable income falls in the supplied bracket.

$\begin{aligned}\text{Excess}&=58\,600-45\,000\\&=\$13\,600\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}\text{Tax payable}&=5092+0.325\times13\,600\\&=5092+4420\\&=\$9512\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}\text{Total instalments}&=350\times26\\&=\$9100\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}\text{Balance}&=9100-9512\\&=-\$412\end{aligned}$
Noah has not paid enough tax, so he owes $\$412.00$.

examples.derivation: 8400 − 7650 = 750: Amelia receives a $750.00 refund. 6200 − 6980 = −780: Ben owes $780.00. 5100 − 5100 = 0: Chen has neither a refund nor an amount owing. These follow the supplied booklet's instalments-minus-tax comparison.
215.50 × 32 = 6896 in actual instalments; 6896 − 6540 = 356. Priya receives a $356.00 refund. Multiplying by the actual pay count follows the booklet's periodic-instalment method.
12480.60 + 1460 = 13940.60 total tax payable. 520 × 26 = 13520 total instalments. 13520 − 13940.60 = −420.60, so Marcus owes $420.60. The Medicare levy is included before the comparison, as taught.
A nil balance requires instalments totalling 14456. Dividing by 26 gives $556.00 per fortnight; 556 × 26 = 14456. This combines the supplied PAYG division method with the year-end balance rule.

58600 lies in the supplied 45001–120000 bracket. Excess = 58600 − 45000 = 13600. Income tax = 5092 + 0.325 × 13600 = 5092 + 4420 = 9512. Instalments = 350 × 26 = 9100. Balance = 9100 − 9512 = −412, so Noah owes $412.00, excluding Medicare as instructed.
